blocks.x: One crying-wolf quarter kills the program; alarm governance is a first-class design goal.

Predictive maintenance fails socially before it fails statistically rests on one claim: enterprises that industrialize measurement ship faster and defend it in audit. The pages that follow show the mechanics, not just the claim.

items: Failure-mode-driven models beat generic anomaly detection: physics before ML.
Predictions must become work orders with parts reserved, or they are dashboard decorations.
Planner trust (share of predictions actioned) is the KPI that predicts program survival.

blocks.x: Three questions to ask your current vendors

items: Ask for the baseline: how was the starting position measured, and who signed it?
Ask for the trail: can your auditors replay any decision the system made last week, end to end?
Ask for the unit cost: what does one decision cost to run, and who owns keeping it down?

blocks.x: We can describe exactly where Predictive maintenance fails socially before it fails statistically programs stall, because we have inherited enough of them: contract-less integrations, drift without owners and dashboards nobody alerts on. The pattern exists to prevent precisely these.

items: Every stage has a gate with real stop authority — scope expands on measured deltas, not on momentum.
The operating model is designed first — who decides what, at which gate, holding which evidence.
Evidence is generated while the work happens, so the audit is a walkthrough, not an archaeology project.

blocks.x: Mature programs run above 70% prediction-action rates with downtime down 30-50%.
